notes: The flagged two-morpheme unit אַף כִּי → *How much more* was re-tested against rule 30 and retained: the a-fortiori pair is one English rendering of which neither morpheme owns a part — no word of *How much more* writes אַף's or כִּי's lexeme in particular — so the condition is met on rule 30's one-rendering reading rather than its one-token reading. The source head is the governing morpheme standing first (rule 23) and the target head the word carrying the comparative force (rule 24).

The competing reading splits the pair, giving *How much more* to the particle and marking the conjunction `unrepresented`; that is what rule 30 forbids for a morpheme whose sense stands inside the fused rendering.
The article assimilated into the pointed בָּ is a real token and takes the written *the* (rule 12).
